isNotAReview: This document reviews no artifact, declares no subject, and carries no verdict, decision, blockingFindingCount or sealRecommendation. It must not be read as a review of any surface.
authority: None. This file is an instrument reading, not a contract. Nothing here may be cited to close a parked recipe, to justify inventing one, or to change any surface disposition. Freeze section 7.6 relies on measurement-only documents being mechanically distinguishable from pins; the six fields above are that distinction.
purpose: Measure one defect class across the whole corpus at once, instead of discovering it one artifact at a time. The class is named in IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md section 5.1: a contract declares an identity/digest-typed field, pins vectors carrying a literal value for it, and states no rule producing that value from real inputs. Every golden passes and the implementer still cannot compute the field.

provenanceOfTheClass.whyASweep: A class found three times by accident warrants one exhaustive measurement. This is the corpus's own derive-don't-enumerate discipline applied to its own gaps.

method.parseDiscipline: Every .json file under artifacts/ was parsed with json.load(fh, object_pairs_hook=H) where H raises on any repeated key, per freeze section 7.5. Measured: 384 documents, 0 parse failures, 0 duplicate-key rejections. THE CORPUS IS LIVE AND MOVED DURING THIS SWEEP: it held 383 .json files at the first read, 384 at the classification pass the totals are stated against, and 386 at the moment this file was written (that last figure includes this file itself). Every intermediate reading was clean. The count is recorded this way rather than as a single number because a stated total that will not reproduce is exactly the kind of carried-forward measurement freeze section 7.2.2 exists to stop.

pinnedPlanDigestConfirmed.note: Measured, not taken on trust. This file was not read, modified or touched beyond hashing it.

method.digestsVerifiedNotTrusted: Every head digest quoted from freeze section 3 was re-measured with shasum -a 256 before its bytes were read. All 21 matched. No digest asserted to this sweep was accepted without measurement.
method.howTheTypeVocabularyWasDerived: Not assumed from any supplied list. Four independent census passes over the corpus, then the union: (1) every distinct string value appearing under a key named type or $ref -- 91 distinct values; (2) every distinct value under wireType, format and fieldType -- 4, 6 and 1 distinct values; (3) every distinct regex under a key whose name contains pattern -- 20 digest-shaped patterns, which is the strongest axis because it is representation-level and name-independent; (4) every distinct textual prefix preceding a 64-hex run anywhere in the corpus -- 213 prefixes, of which 13 are identity schemes rather than prose. The key named kind (6013 occurrences) was examined and EXCLUDED: its 272 values are record discriminators such as verifier-manifest and predicate-semantics, not type declarations. Field-name morphology was used only to widen the candidate net, never to classify.
method.howPositionsWereFound: Two complementary sweeps whose union was taken, so a field missed by one axis is still caught. (a) Declaration-driven: every field name appearing in a field-list structure (fields, orderedFields, requiredFields, optionalFields, closedTypes, digestFields, preimageFields, exactFields and 14 further spellings discovered by key census) or as a key whose value is a type-declaring object -- 1272 distinct declared field names. (b) Occurrence-driven: every object key anywhere in the corpus carrying at least one digest-shaped value under the derived pattern vocabulary -- 906 distinct keys corpus-wide, 171 on the binding heads.
method.howAbsenceWasEstablished: For every LITERAL-ONLY row below, absence of a rule was established by search, never assumed. The standard applied: a programmatic walk of all 384 parsed documents collecting (i) every occurrence of the field name as a KEY, and (ii) every occurrence of the field name INSIDE any string value, then intersecting (ii) with rule-vocabulary (preimage, domainSeparator, domainUtf8, canonicaliz, SHA-256(, is computed, derived as, recipe, byte recipe, encoding). A row is LITERAL-ONLY only when that intersection is empty or contains solely embedding rules rather than producing rules. The searches are recorded per row.
method.rulesWereExecutedNotOnlyRead: Where a rule was found, it was implemented from the quoted text alone and run against the corpus's own pinned values. Reproductions performed by this sweep are recorded in reproductionsPerformed below. A stated rule that could not be executed is reported as stated-but-unverified, not as computable.
method.namesAreNotNatures: Classification is by what the corpus SAYS, never by suffix. Applied in both directions: requestId ends in Id and is digest-shaped but is COMPUTABLE-BY-ALLOCATION because the corpus states a CSPRNG allocation rule; profileId ends in Id but is a closed label and needs no recipe; unitSetCommitment has zero prose occurrences of its own name yet is COMPUTABLE because the governing rule sits in the sibling key unitSetCommitmentRecipe; and executionPlanCommitment carries a realistic digest and a required-field declaration yet has no producing rule anywhere.

typeVocabularyDerived.vocabularyItemsNotInTheSuppliedPrompt: The prompt suggested $ref Digest, sha256Id, ...Id, ...Commitment, ...Digest, ...Ref. Derivation from the corpus additionally produced: ContentDigest, Sha256Text, OpaqueId, CanonicalValueRef, RawObjectKeyV1, the RawCasRef<...> and SemanticCommitmentRef<...> parameterised families, the prose-named EP and RT commitment types, and eighteen wire patterns including three (root1-, purge1-, migrate1-) that no name-suffix heuristic would reach. ContentDigest and OpaqueId each turned out to carry a LITERAL-ONLY member, so deriving rather than assuming the vocabulary was load-bearing, not ceremonial.

scope.surfacesSwept: The 21 binding surfaces named in IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 3, plus the 3 candidate identity-recipe artifacts, because a delegation chain that ends in a literal is still a member of the class and two of the three chains run through the candidates.
scope.predecessorsRead: Where a head is a delta document or has shed a grammar, the predecessor carrying the rule was read and is named in the row. This was necessary for C-2 (v9 is a delta over v4), EVALUATION-PROOF (v13 carries no commitment grammar; v5-v9 do) and RETENTION (v24 dropped three grammars present in v15-v22).
scope.architectureDirectory: architecture/*.md was examined and contributes NO declared identity-typed field position. Measured: the twelve files mention identity names in prose only (planIntentCommitment 5, universeCommitment 2, outcomeSetDigest 2, and eight others once each) and declare no wire type, pattern or preimage. IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md line 105 classes architecture/ as narrative that governs only where it does not conflict. It is therefore in scope and empty, not out of scope and unexamined.

excludedWithReason.corpusSelfPins: Digests of files in this repository (sha256, checkerSha256, artifactSha256, sourceSha256, independentReviewSha256, sha256Measured, expectedPin, predecessorSha256 and 40 further spellings) are NOT members of the class. Their rule is sha256 of named bytes, and this was verified rather than assumed: 2603 (file, digest) pairs were resolved and re-hashed against live bytes, of which 2310 match exactly. The 293 that differ are time-indexed review snapshots pinning bytes as they stood at review time, which is the intended behaviour of a pin and not a defect. These are excluded from the totals because an implementer can always compute them, and including ~400 of them would drown the signal.
excludedWithReason.documentSelfMeasurement: Structures such as c2-plan-stage-schema.v9#/documentSkeleton/subtrees map a top-level key name to the sha256 of that subtree. Computable by construction; excluded for the same reason.

states.COMPUTABLE: A rule producing the value from real inputs is stated on a surface an implementer builds against.
states.DELEGATED: The rule lives on a different surface this one imports by reference. Each such row names the surface AND states whether that surface's rule is itself computable, because a delegation chain ending in a literal is a member of the class.
states.LITERAL-ONLY: No rule anywhere in the corpus. Every occurrence is a constant in a vector, fixture, golden or example. This is the class.
states.COMPUTABLE-BY-ALLOCATION: The corpus states the value is minted (CSPRNG or host allocation) rather than derived. An implementer can produce it, so it is NOT a member of the class. Recorded separately because a derivation rule would be WRONG here, not missing.
states.LABEL-NOT-DIGEST: Carries an identity-looking name but the corpus types it as a closed label or enum and never asks for a recipe. Not a member of the class.

placeholderTellFindings.question: Did the sweep find a LITERAL-ONLY field carrying a realistic-looking digest -- the dangerous case the tell would miss?
placeholderTellFindings.answer: YES. Six of them, and they are the highest-consequence findings in this document.
placeholderTellFindings.method: Every candidate value was scored by nibble distribution over its 64-hex body: a value was called a placeholder when one nibble occupies 48 or more of 64 positions or the value uses 4 or fewer distinct nibbles; low-entropy at 24+ or 8 or fewer distinct; realistic otherwise. Scoring was applied to all values, and classification never depended on it.
literalOnlyFieldsWithRealisticDigests: executionPlanCommitment -- sha256:7c3174f6... (88 sites) and sha256:dca3a310... (51 sites)
indexFingerprint -- sha256:2c235fac... (9 sites, pinned on a binding head)
coverageId -- sha256:f218fc19... and sha256:5bcd0f8a... on the superseded surface
factPartitionRef -- sha256:2f0ad0ca... and sha256:a11fe97e... in evidence.v3
placeholderTellFindings.conclusion: The repeated-nibble tell is a useful signal and an unsafe filter. It fires on capabilityManifestId, derivationDigest, sealedManifestDigest, FactViewId and the resolved-inputs leaves -- and misses every one of the six above. Two of those six have rules that exist only in checker Python, which no grep over JSON contracts would ever surface. This is the concrete reason the task required a sweep rather than a grep, and the measurement confirms the premise.
placeholderTellFindings.inverseCaseAlsoFound: Realistic values are equally weak evidence of computability in the other direction: subjectScopeCommitment's seven values are all realistic AND it is computable, while evidenceDigest carries both realistic values and a sha256:dddd... placeholder across its four.

structuralFinding_headsHaveShedTheirGram.statement: Independently on two surfaces, the current head retains the identity LITERALS while having dropped the GRAMMAR that makes them computable.
structuralFinding_headsHaveShedTheirGram.retention: retention-tiers.v24.json carries 4194 recordCasRef literals and 42 distinct digests, and no longer contains SEMANTIC-CAPABILITY-CLOSURE-GRAMMAR-V3, OPERATIONAL-CUSTODY-PROJECTION-CANONICAL-JSON-V1 or RT15-RAW-BYTES-PRIMARY-V1, all present in v15-v22. Measured: grep -c returns 0 on v24 for all three.
structuralFinding_headsHaveShedTheirGram.evaluationProof: evaluation-proof.v13.json has 32 top-level keys and none is canonicalCommitmentGrammar, normativePreimageGrammar, preimageGoldens or rawAuthorityRecordGrammar. Those existed in v5-v9 and were dropped at v10. v13 is a guard/measurement artifact whose declared role is repairing IR-EP11-01 and IR-EP12-01.
structuralFinding_headsHaveShedTheirGram.whyItMatters: An implementer building against the freeze section 3 head set alone cannot compute several fields that ARE computable elsewhere in the corpus. C-2 handles the same situation correctly by declaring at v9 /derivedFrom that the effective contract is the verified predecessor plus the listed operations. evaluation-proof.v13 declares only supersedesProofObligationsOf, and retention-tiers.v24 carries a 7-pointer carriedFragments subset. This is not itself a member of the measured class and is recorded because it changes who can compute what, and because it is invisible to any per-field search.

nonDiscriminatingVectors.purpose: Cases where a rule IS stated and the pinned vector cannot distinguish two readings of it. These are not members of the measured class; they are the adjacent failure where a green suite proves less than it appears to.
cases: promptTextDigest -- the rule says 'SHA-256 of the exact disclosure text' with no encoding and no normalization named. The disclosure text is pure ASCII, so the vector cannot discriminate NFC from raw, nor UTF-8 from anything else. A non-ASCII disclosure would fork implementations and no vector would catch it.
subjectScopeCommitment -- RFC 7049 and RFC 8949 CBOR key orderings coincide for text keys shorter than 24 bytes, so the fixture cannot discriminate them.
evaluationProofBundleCasRef -- the single reproduction was over a pure-ASCII bundle and cannot distinguish key-sort by Unicode scalar value from key-sort by UTF-8 bytes, which differ above the BMP.
semanticCapabilityClosureCasRef -- sorted-keys reproduces the pin and insertion-order does not; the corpus never states which, and no vector exposes the fork.

whatThisSweepCannotSee.preamble: A false negative here is worse than a false positive, because it reads as coverage. These are the boundaries of what the measurement establishes.
limits: PROSE RULES THAT NAME NO FIELD. Absence was established by intersecting field-name occurrences with rule vocabulary. A derivation stated in prose that never names the field and uses none of the search terms would not be caught. This is a real gap: unitSetCommitment has ZERO prose occurrences of its own name and is nonetheless computable via a sibling key, which proves the failure mode exists. It was caught only because the sibling key was inspected by hand.

RULES IN EXECUTABLE CODE. This sweep read *.py only to confirm two specific absences from JSON. It did NOT systematically sweep the 94 checkers for derivations that exist only in code. rawBytesCommitment, fixtureCommitment and indexFingerprint were each found this way, so the class is known to be non-empty and its true size in the checker corpus is UNMEASURED. That is the single largest known blind spot in this document.

SEMANTIC CORRECTNESS. Reproducing a pinned value proves a rule executes as written. It does not prove the rule is the RIGHT one, that its input set is complete for a real project, or that two conforming implementations agree on inputs the vectors do not exercise. See nonDiscriminatingVectors.

NON-JSON SURFACES. architecture/*.md was examined and contributes no declared position. The remaining .md files (freeze, blueprint, TREE-ENDSTATE, v1-slice, agent logs, steering/, cleansheet/, deltas/) were read only where cited. A field declared solely in Markdown prose would be missed.

SUPERSEDED-LINEAGE COMPLETENESS. Classification targeted the 21 heads plus 3 candidates, reading predecessors where a head is a delta or has shed a grammar. Roughly 360 further documents -- earlier versions, reviews, adjudications -- were parsed and value-swept but not exhaustively classified. A rule present ONLY in an unread superseded document could make a LITERAL-ONLY row wrong in the safe direction (over-reporting), and a field declared only there could make the sweep incomplete in the unsafe direction.

THE OPAQUE-IDENTIFIER SUBCLASS IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A VERDICT. For the six OpaqueId-typed positions this document records that the corpus states NEITHER a derivation NOR that the value is caller- or host-supplied. It does NOT assert each needs a digest recipe. Several may need only an explicit supply statement. Treating all six as identical to capabilityManifestId would overstate the finding.

A LIVE CORPUS. The document count moved from 383 to 384 during this sweep. All digests were re-measured at read time, but any artifact changed after this file was written is outside what it establishes.

NO INDEPENDENT REPLICATION. Reproductions recorded here were performed once, by this sweep. Where a value was reproduced the encoder was written from the quoted prose alone, but no second independent encoder was written, so the standard set by evidence-identity-recipes (two encoders, zero disagreements) is NOT met by this document.

TOTALS ARE A CLASSIFICATION COUNT, NOT A CENSUS. positionsExamined counts positions that reached classification. It is not the count of every digest-valued key in the corpus, which is 906, most of them corpus self-pins excluded with reason above.
